calls.reason: The claim is probabilistic. Brown's training report and the 2019 Wikipedia page make repeated exposure plausible, but neither establishes experiment-specific inclusion or sampling.
The packet found no qualifying retraining experiment, but the forecast has no deadline. Absence of a study so far does not decide whether one will happen.
The percentages come only from Marcus and Davis's own report, with no independent audit. Its differing totals of 157 and 80 tests also leave the comparison uncertain.
SpartQA and PIQA establish some coverage, while Melnik's survey identifies gaps. None establishes whether most forms were untested or whether broad commonsense measurement was reliable.

Bang and Sap document spatial and social failures, but Bang finds stronger temporal results and Kosinski reports 93% on selected false-belief tasks. The evidence does not clearly settle the broad claim.

OpenAI's InstructGPT paper reports preference and truthfulness gains alongside regressions on several benchmarks, including translation. This directly supports the main point that overall improvement can be uneven.
